newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: SOCCER SHOWCASE-ZAGALLO NO QUALMS ABOUT PLAYING UGLY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-ZAGALLO NO QUALMS ABOUT PLAYING UGLY.

text.p: Brazil coach Mario Zagallo said on Saturday that winning was his main aim and he had no qualms about acheving it by playing ugly football.
"The most important thing in football is the result," said Zagallo, whose comments will make depressing reading for soccer fans worldwide.

"Everyone wants to win and I am no different. I like to win using artistic football but sometimes the best way to win is using other methods. It depends on the opponents, sometimes it is they who decide."

The veteran coach candidly admitted that he had adopted a cautious tactical scheme in Thursday's Copa America first round game against Colombia, when his team gave an insomnia-curing display in a 2-0 win which saw Brazil's opponents play most of the good football.
He refused to disclose whether he would repeat the defensive approach for Sunday's quarter-final against Paraguay but admitted the possibility had crossed his mind.

"I'm not going to tell you whether we will play as we did in the second half against Mexico or like we did against Colombia," said Zagallo, whose team gave an enthralling display as they came from 2-0 down to beat Mexico 3-2 Monday.
"We can follow two paths and we will follow the one which is best for us on the day."

Zagallo is forced to make at least one change for Sunday's game, which is likely to represent a stiff challenge for his team. Full back Cafu, suspended after picking up his second yellow card against Colombia, will be replaced by Ze Maria.

Elsewhere, Zagallo refused to comment on his line-up, the only certainty being that Ronaldo and Romario will as usual form the attack. The centre of the defence has been Zagallo's biggest headache and he has tried several combinations in the team's recent games.
Paraguay, who blamed the altitude in Cochabamba for their disappointing first round performance when they finished third in their group, have several injury problems.
Midfielder Estanislao Struway is definitely ruled out and the Paraguayans also have injuries to two central defenders, Celso Ayala and Ricardo Rojas.

Goalkeeper Jose Luis Chilavert, who suffered a knock in Tuesday's draw against Argentina when he scored from a penalty, appeared to have recovered on Friday, when he was practising free kicks as usual.
Paraguay's Brazilian coach Paulo Cesar Carpegiani said he was not worried about Brazil's so-called "Ro-Ro" attack.
"We're not frightened by the thought of playing Brazil," he said. "We're not going to have man-to-man marking on Ronaldo or any other striker."

Paraguay lead the South American World Cup group, where they have lost only once in 10 games, but they have not faced Brazil in the competition because the world champions qualify automatically for France next year.
